overview.text: The Notice Inviting Tender (NIT) No. 04/EE/CED-IV/CCU/Kol/2024-25 is issued by the Executive Engineer, CED-IV, CCU, MoEF&CC, Kolkata.

The work involves Construction of open dais, Green room & washrooms at Phool bagan in front of CESC Garden and Repairing/replacement of 2km barbed wire on the boundary wall of AJCBIBG from Howrah main gate to bakultala gate during the year 2024-25.
The estimated cost put to bid is Rs. 49,61,435.00/- for Civil & Electrical works.
An Earnest Money Deposit (EMD) of Rs. 99,229.00/- is required.
The period of completion is 06 (Six) Months.
Bids are invited from CPWD enlisted contractors in Buildings & Roads category and firms/contractors of repute in a single bid system via online percentage rate bids.
The last date and time for submission of the bid is 3 PM on 14/01/2025.

The NIT is for 'Construction of open dais, Green room & washrooms at Phool bagan in front of CESC Garden and Repairing, replacement of 2km barbed wire on the boundary wall of AJCBIBG from Howrah main gate to bakultala gate during the year 2024-25'.
The work is estimated to cost Rs. 49,61,435.00/-.
The financial bid shall be opened at 03:30 PM on 14/01/2025.
Issuing organization is Executive Engineer, CED-IV, CCU (For and on behalf of the President of India).
The RFP invites percentage rate bids from approved CPWD registered contractors for the construction of open dais, green room, and washrooms at Phool Bagan in front of CESC Garden.
The RFP also covers the repairing and replacement of 2km of barbed wire on the boundary wall of AJCBIBG from Howrah main gate to Bakultala gate.
The work is estimated to cost Rs. 49,61,435.00/- as a rough guide.
The financial bid is scheduled to be opened at 03:30 PM on January 14, 2025.
Issuing organization is the President of India on behalf of CPWD (Central Public Works Department).

The tender is for the construction of open dais, green room, and washrooms at Phool bagan in front of CESC Garden, and repair/replacement of 2km barbed wire on the boundary wall of AJCBIBG from Howrah main gate to Bakultala gate during the year 2024-25.
The tendering process requires online bid submission by 3 PM on 14/01/2025.
Tender opening is scheduled for 3:30 PM on 14/01/2025 in the office of the Executive Engineer, CED-IV, CCU, MoEF&CC, AJCB Indian Botanic Garden.
The issuing organization is the Ministry of Environment, Forest & Climate Change (MoEF&CC) represented by the Executive Engineer, CED-IV, Civil Construction Unit.
This notice inviting bid forms part of the contract document.
The document is an annexure containing forms and guarantees for contract execution by a contractor (CCU) on behalf of the Government.
It includes a Bank Guarantee Form for Earnest Money Deposit/Performance Guarantee/Security Deposit to be offered by a bank.
The validity period of the guarantee depends on the bid system: 90 days for financial bids and 180 days for two/three bid systems.
The agreement is supplementary to Contract No. ……….. dated ………………, between the Guarantor (Contractor) and the President of India (Government).
The contract concerns sanitary installations and water supply works.
The tenderer must provide and maintain approaches from the main road or improve existing approaches at their own cost without additional payment.
The contractor must obtain all necessary licenses for temporary obstructions and enclosures while paying associated fees to local authorities.
No payment shall be made for any damage caused by natural calamities such as rain, snowfall, or flood during work execution.
The work should be planned in a systematic manner to minimize chase cuttings in walls, ceilings, and floors.
Chases will not be allowed to be cut using hammer or chisel; use of machin es is required wherever absolutely essential.
Contractor must coordinate disciplines such as sanitary, water supply, electric, and fire-fighting services.
The contractor is responsible for watching and guarding buildings against pilferage and breakage until physical handover.
The tender is for Electrical (E) & Mechanical (M) works including installation, wiring, conduits, switches, fixtures, and related systems.
All work is to be executed in strict accordance with specifications, approved designs, drawings, and instructions of the Engineer-in-Charge.

If equipment supplied for work during the currency of the earlier Associate Contractor and paid partly by the Department becomes redundant due to a change in agency, the Main Contractor shall be liable for replacement at no cost to the Department.
No change of Associated Contractor will be allowed without prior approval of the Engineer-in-charge of the work.
The project involves the construction of an open dais, Green room, and washrooms at Phool bagan in front of CESC Garden.
The project also includes repairing and replacing 2km of barbed wire on the boundary wall of AJCBIBG from Howrah main gate to bakultala gate during the year 2024-25.
The tender documents indicate a contract period of one year (2024-25).

scope.text: Major Component includes Civil work, specifically construction of open dais, green room, washrooms, and replacement of 2km barbed wire on the boundary wall.
Minor Component includes Electrical work.
The Major Component of work is Civil Work and Minor Component of work is Electrical Work.
The main contractor shall execute the minor component(s) also or associate himself with an eligible agency for execution of electrical work.
Time allowed for carrying out the work will be 08 (Eight) months from the date of start as defined in schedule 'F' or from the first date of handing over of the site, whichever is later.
Architectural drawings shall be made available in phased manner, as per requirement and approved programme.
Construction of open dais, green room & washrooms at Phool bagan in front of CESC Garden.
Repairing and replacement of 2km barbed wire on the boundary wall of AJCBIBG from Howrah main gate to bakultala gate.
The Bank Guarantee covers compliance of contractor obligations, payment demands up to the specified amount, and enforcement by the Government without proceeding against the contractor first.
The guarantor (bank) cannot revoke the guarantee except with the consent of the Government in writing.
Annexure II covers a ten-year warranty by the contractor for waterproofing works, excluding defects caused by earthquakes or misuse.
Annexure III covers a five-year warranty by the contractor for sanitary installations and water supply works, excluding defects caused by misuse or structural issues.
Work must be carried out in compliance with relevant bylaws, regulations, and directives of the Engineer-in-charge.
Rates for all items are considered inclusive of labour, material, tools, plant, heights, depths, leads, carriages, and pumping/baling out water if necessary.
Contractor rates apply to construction executed in two or more shifts including night work where site conditions demand it.
RCC, electrical, and finishing work are normally not allowed at night unless site circumstances so demand.
Contractor must ensure proper coordination of various disciplines viz. sanitary & water supply, electrical, fire-fighting and any other services.
Existing drains, pipes, cables, over-head wires, sewer lines, water lines and similar services encountered shall be protected against damage at contractor's expense.
In case existing services are to be removed and diverted, the same shall be payable to the contractor upon approval by Engineer-in-Charge.
Contractor must work out the cost of removal and diversion and obtain approval from Engineer-in-Charge.
Contractor shall not store materials or occupy site in a manner likely to hinder operation of services.
Testing charges are borne by the contractor unless specified otherwise.
Hidden items such as water supply lines, drainage pipes, electrical conduits, and sewers must be properly tested before covering as per design conditions.
The contractor must give a performance test of the entire installation(s) as per standing specifications before final acceptance.
Scope includes providing copies of challans, cash memos, receipts, vouchers, and manufacturer certificates for materials procured upon Department request.
Site cleanliness requires removing muck, rubbish, and building material to approved dumping grounds per local byelaws.
Excavated earth or building rubbish shall not be stacked on areas where other buildings, roads, services, or compound walls are to be constructed.
The contractor is responsible for providing potable water and minimum sanitation/safety facilities for workers.
Special scope covers the use of OPC conforming to IS: 8112 or PPC conforming to IS: 1489 (Part 1) from preferred makes.
Cement must be supplied in 50 kg bags with manufacturer's name, ISI marking, and grade/type specifications.
The contractor must construct a cement godown with minimum capacity of 200 bags at the site of work.
Special conditions for steel reinforcement require ISI marked TMT bars of various grades from preferred makes or authorized dealers.
Steel reinforcement bars must be supplied to the site in bulk supply of 25 tonnes or more as decided by the Engineer-in-charge.
The scope includes electrical installation of conduits, wiring, modular switches, MCBs, MCCBs, DBs, fans, fixtures, UPS, EPABX, Krone Boxes, and Audio-Video Conferencing systems.
Work covers laying conduit, fish wiring, earthing, interconnection, and provision of junction boxes for pulling wires.
Scope includes providing land accommodation for labour, temporary workshops, approach roads, and storage of materials at the site.
For all works, including Electrical installations, materials shall be procured only from original equipment manufacturers/authorized dealers of OEM.
Contractor must arrange land for accommodation of labour, setting up of office, storage of materials, and construction of approach roads at site expense.
Work shall not interfere or adversely affect other works being executed by other agencies, and any damage caused to existing or other agency works must be made good by the contractor.
All routine tests on equipment must be conducted before dispatch from manufacturers' premises.
Supplying and wiring light points, fan points, exhaust fan points, and call bell points using 1.5 sq.mm FRLS PVC insulated copper conductor single core cable.
Supplying and wiring group controlled (looped) light points, fan points, exhaust fan points, and call bell points without independent switches.
Supplying and fixing horizontal type three pole and neutral sheet steel MCB distribution boards for 415 volts on surface or recess.
Supplying and laying 1.1 KV grade PVC insulated, PVC sheathed, or XLPE power cables in existing RCC/HUME/METAL pipes.
Supplying and laying DWC HDPE pipes (63mm dia) direct in ground including excavation and refilling.

key_requirements.text: Bidders must submit detail of associated agencies for specialized component(s) to Engineer-in-Charge within prescribed time.

Main Contractor/Associate must submit all equipment, accessories, shop floor drawings, catalogues, and make/model lists for approval prior to placing orders.

Contractor must submit a Quality Assurance Manual including the Quality Assurance Plan & Checklist for E&M Service.
Agency must provide storage cum erection insurance and third-party insurance covering transit, storage, erection, and commissioning from storage to handing over.
All items must confirm to e-waste management and handling rules issued by the Ministry of Environment and Forest, Government of India.
All items must comply with ROHS restrictions on use of hazardous substances or WEEE compliant as per EU norms or American norms.
Material shall not be older by more than six months from the date of supply at site.
Proof of dispatch from factory/dealer shall always be submitted to Engineer-in-charge for verification.

The percentage quoted shall appear in two decimal places.

eligibility.text: Bidders must declare that eligible similar work(s) has/have not been executed through another contractor on a back-to-back basis to avoid future debarment in CCU, MoEF&CC.
Associated agencies must conform to eligibility criteria as defined in the bid document and be approved by the Engineer-in-Charge.
The contractor must execute a supplementary guarantee agreement for defect removal after completion of waterproofing or sanitary works.
For waterproofing works, the contractor is liable for leakage only if not caused by earthquakes, structural defects, or roof misuse.
For sanitary and water supply works, the contractor is liable for defects excluding those caused by misuse.
The contractor must indemnify the Department against claims arising from violations of laws, patent rights, royalties, or damages to adjacent buildings caused by them or their employees.
No claim whatsoever shall be entertained for extra costs incurred during night shifts or pandemic/epidemic conditions including COVID-19 arrangements.
Existing drains, pipes, cables, over-head wires, sewer lines, and water lines must be protected by the contractor at their own expense.
The tenderer must either satisfy eligibility conditions for E&M components themselves or associate with agencies fulfilling these requirements.
Proposals to associate an agency must be submitted in Form 'B' of the tender document from each associate independently.
Eligibility decision requires submission of registration documents, Electrical License, and GST Documents duly attested by applicants to Executive Engineer CED-IV CCU.
Associated contractors must certify they are not debarred as on the day of application for tender participation.
No change of Associated Contractor is allowed without prior approval of the Engineer-in-charge.
